summary: Modern security architectures shift from perimeter-based models to Zero Trust frameworks, emphasizing continuous authorization and the principle of least privilege. These systems integrate advanced defensive mechanisms like behavioral analytics, cryptographic privacy preservation, and hardware-level hardening to mitigate vulnerabilities, while acknowledging the fundamental limitations of trust in software supply chains.
title: Zero Trust Security, Privacy, and System Hardening

fun_fact_idea.exciting_angle: Connect Ken Thompson's 'Reflections on Trusting Trust' to modern software supply chain attacks like the SolarWinds hack. This shows the student that the most sophisticated security engineering is still vulnerable to foundational trust issues in the tools we use to build our code.
